Description: **Azure Application Gateways** are evaluated for **HTTP/2** support on client connections (`enableHttp2`). The gateway offers HTTP/2 only over TLS on HTTPS listeners, and traffic to backend pools always uses HTTP/1.1.
Risk: Clients fall back to **HTTP/1.1**, opening more TLS connections and losing HTTP/2 multiplexing and header compression. The direct security impact is low, so treat this as protocol hygiene and performance rather than an exposure.

Code.Other:
1. In the Azure portal, open the Application Gateway
2. Under Settings, select Configuration
3. Set HTTP2 to Enabled and click Save

Recommendation.Text: Enable **HTTP/2** on every gateway so clients that support it negotiate the modern protocol over TLS. HTTP/1.1 clients keep working because the gateway supports both.

Notes: The Azure API leaves HTTP/2 disabled unless it is set, while the Azure portal enables it by default.
